learningObjective: Reason about when two nested loops in a loop-level IR can be safely interchanged based on the affine access patterns of the loop body.

canonicalClaims.claim: Loop interchange preserves semantics iff no dependence direction vector in the original loop nest becomes illegal after the swap; loops with no loop-carried dependences (e.g., pure elementwise stores over disjoint iteration coordinates) permit any permutation.
conditions: The IR supports affine access-pattern analysis or an equivalent dependence-testing framework.
The transformation preserves the original iteration domain.
nonImplications: Does not imply legal interchange is always beneficial (cache locality varies).
Does not imply interchange is the only reordering; skewing, tiling, fission are related but different.

misconceptions.whyWrong: Loop-carried dependences can be violated by the swap; dependence analysis is required.

misconceptions.claim: Only square loop nests (M == N) can be interchanged.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Loop bounds are irrelevant to interchange legality; only dependence directions matter.
Interchange is defined on rolled loops.

misconceptions.claim: Interchange changes what is computed by the loop nest.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Interchange preserves the compute; it changes only the iteration order.

implementationFacts: MLIR affine analysis: dependence testing via affine access maps
Dependence direction vectors: `<, =, >` per loop dim; interchange must keep all vectors lexicographically legal
For elementwise nests with disjoint iteration reads/writes, interchange is unconditionally safe
performanceScenarios: Interchange changes memory access order; effect on locality depends on layout.
